quotes.text: Customer location refers to the country where the customer’s bank account is held.
the payment fails with the error code `payment_method_provider_timeout`.
It combines an initial Pay by Bank payment with a [Bacs Direct Debit](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/bacs-debit.md) mandate for recurring payments.

old_evidence.text: Pay by Bank for customers in France, Germany, and Ireland is in private preview.
Express Checkout Element and Mobile Payment Element don’t support Pay by Bank.

findings: Both product overviews document a customer-initiated, single-use open-banking payment approved through the bank's app or portal, GBP/EUR, £0.50–£10,000 default GBP transaction range, standard payout timing, no manual capture and Connect (old lines 8-54; new lines 9-59). The 35 Stripe account business locations remain the same (old 60-98; new 65-103), distinct from customer bank-account locations and Checkout-route requirements.

Source lines 17 and 27 require dated correction: Ireland moves from May preview to November general availability alongside Finland and the UK, and Belgium joins France and Germany in private preview. November enumerates the banks by account-held country and UK GBP versus listed European EUR (new lines 17-27, 61-67, 115-217; old lines 14-22, 56-62). The preview form heading names France/Germany; broader prose includes Belgium. A form or sign-in/request is not approval.

Source lines 23-35 should surface the scoped November no-chargeback wording, final refund lifecycle, late-transfer failure, and account capability prerequisites. Browser redirect or authorization is not verified payment success, funds availability or payout. New lines 248-264 retain the asynchronous refund states and add late-bank-transfer behavior; new lines 279-293 retain the historical Connect capability paths.

Root index line 7 routes via Stripe index lines 352-354 and 748 to the real-time payments concept lines 18, 34-36, 87-101 and 217-218; stale undated customer, mobile and recurring language needs reciprocal product and integration routes.
substantive_changes: New lines 17-27 and 61-217 explicitly separate bank account and merchant location, add Belgium to customer-access preview, move Ireland to general availability, and add a country-specific supported-bank directory. The same institution overseas is insufficient.

New lines 260-264 document possible `payment_method_provider_timeout` after bank authorization if Stripe does not receive funds within the expected settlement window. Stripe automatically returns funds that arrive after failure. Keep that distinct from a merchant-initiated refund or a payout.

New lines 266-277 describe separate request-access private preview for Elements/PaymentIntents users, combining a first Pay by Bank payment with a Bacs Direct Debit mandate for subsequent recurring payments. Comparative first-payment, dispute, bank verification and within-three-business-day payout statements occur in that preview context. They do not override standard payout timing for the one-off product.

New lines 105-113 retain Checkout subscription-mode and Express Checkout Element exclusions while dropping the express May Mobile Payment Element exclusion (old 100-108). New lines 256-258 articulate no chargeback for ordinary goods/services disputes; do not infer a guarantee against all recourse or extend the first-payment clause to the Bacs mandate.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Preserve May 6, 2026 country, no recurring and no Mobile Payment Element statements as dated (old lines 14-34, 56-62, 100-108), along with separate full old provenance.

Both retain Dashboard enablement for front-end products, dynamic relevance and a manual route pointer (old lines 131-138, new lines 239-246), plus Connect direct, destination and separate charges and transfers. Connected accounts using Dashboard manage payment settings and verify `capabilities.pay_by_bank_payments` active through Accounts API or webhooks; Express/non-Stripe dashboards request through Capabilities API. A request is distinct from approval/active status (old 152-166; new 279-293).

Both retain 730-day full/partial refunds to original bank account, no refund fee and original processing fee non-refundable. Follow `refund.updated` or `refund.failed` and Refund object `succeeded`/`failed`; failure sends amount back to Stripe balance and requires an alternate refund (old 140-146; new 248-254).
conflicts: April 20 Checkout Dashboard migration capture includes Pay by Bank among delayed notification methods and advises waiting for success or failure when completion represents authorization (raw/stripe-checkout-dashboard-payment-methods-2025.md:1-5, 66-84; wiki/sources/source-stripe-checkout-dashboard-payment-methods.md:12-32). May 6 acceptance guide says immediate success/failure notification for Pay by Bank (raw/stripe-pay-by-bank-accept-payment-2025.md:12,139). Keep reciprocal warnings and use the November product timeout as distinct companion evidence. General 2–14 day wording is not a Pay by Bank SLA. Distinguish authorization, browser return, verified success, funds availability and payout.

May method overview explicitly excludes Mobile Payment Element (old lines 100-108). November method text drops that exclusion without independently asserting mobile support (new 105-113), while November real-time product matrix changes its May unsupported cell to supported (raw/stripe-real-time-payments-2025.md:24-26; raw/stripe-payments-real-time-2026-11-07.md:25-34). Date the independent matrix and avoid extrapolating universal mobile account or SDK availability.

Distinguish the November Bacs-backed recurring preview from real-time matrix `send_invoice` Invoicing/Subscriptions and unsupported SetupIntents/`setup_future_usage` (raw/stripe-payments-real-time-2026-11-07.md:25-40) and the separately versioned `2026-02-25.clover` Billing API enum change (raw/stripe-changelog-clover-2026-02-25-billing-api-pay-by-bank-2026-11-07.md:1-23, 63-74). The changelog's recurring billing language establishes neither automatic collection for one-off Pay by Bank nor broad access to the Bacs-backed Elements preview. Method overview still excludes Checkout subscription mode.
unresolved_questions: Exact account/variant eligibility, current supported banks, and notification or payout timing for a specific payment cannot be verified from these captures. The France/Germany interest form heading does not resolve Belgium's request route.

findings: Preserve both dated product snapshots. Fix lines 17, 23 and 27-35 with customer-bank versus merchant geography, bank routes, Bacs-backed private preview versus one-off and Billing, refund state, late transfer/timeouts and Connect activation. Preserve unchanged GBP bounds, merchant location count and standard payout.
conflicts: Reciprocally link April delayed Checkout guidance and May acceptance immediate-notification wording with November timeout qualification; keep Mobile Payment Element evidence and Billing/API version distinct and dated.
source_assessments.reason: The November method overview changes availability and adds meaningful failure and recurring-preview behavior. The May-only summary's mobile, recurring and flow shorthand would mislead queries if used without dated scope.

answers.Q1: The November capture for https://docs.stripe.com/payments/pay-by-bank describes customer-initiated, single-use open-banking payments approved in the customer's bank app or portal. Bank accounts in Finland, Ireland and the UK are generally available, while Belgium, France and Germany require preview access; UK accounts pay GBP and listed European accounts EUR. This differs from the May customer locations and preview list; eligible Stripe business locations remain separate (new raw lines 9-67, new raw lines 105-217, old raw lines 8-62 and old raw lines 64-98). There is no manual capture, and standard payout timing applies. A bank authorization can still fail with `payment_method_provider_timeout`; after failure late funds are automatically returned, separately from the 730-day merchant refund route and its final states. The Elements/PaymentIntents private preview uses an initial Pay by Bank payment and a Bacs Direct Debit mandate for subsequent payments (new raw lines 37-59 and new raw lines 248-277). Connect charge routes persist, and Dashboards or the Capabilities API are used according to account access. Check the capability is active via Accounts API or webhooks (old raw lines 152-166 and new raw lines 279-293). source-stripe-pay-by-bank.md accurately preserves several May facts but needs dated country, mobile, recurring and outcome qualifications.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/pay-by-bank, the redesigned asset links and Elements quickstart are presentation or navigation (old raw lines 110-138 and new raw lines 219-246). November substantively adds Belgium preview, Ireland general availability, bank-account-specific supported banks, the authorized-but-failed timeout and late-funds return, and a Bacs-backed Elements/PaymentIntents recurring private preview (old raw lines 14-34, old raw lines 56-62, new raw lines 17-27, new raw lines 115-217 and new raw lines 260-277). Preserve May no recurring and mobile exclusion as dated in source-stripe-pay-by-bank.md (old raw lines 30-34 and old raw lines 100-108). November's method overview omits the mobile exclusion, while the separate real-time matrix affirmatively lists mobile support. That evidence does not specify all SDK versions or merchant availability. Keep Checkout subscription mode excluded, Billing API `2026-02-25.clover` enum support and the matrix's `send_invoice` scope separate from the Bacs mandate preview. Reciprocally warn that April's Dashboard migration guide lists delayed notification while the May acceptance guide describes immediate notification. The November timeout shows why bank authorization, user return, verified success, funds availability and payout differ; neither source guarantees a universal immediate outcome or a method-specific 2–14 day window.
